entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: The Good Sponge
entries.body: i chose the white sponge because it made me look fragile. A small fish examined the arrangement for a long time. I did not move. It left with a compliment and all its organs.
entries.sceneFit: The pale frogfish is visibly perched in white sponge, the exact vanity-and-ambush tableau.
entries.payoffReview: His aesthetic self-regard loses to an absurdly polite failure. The fish survives because he cannot break the pose.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: Firm Ground
entries.body: i put both little feet down on the sand and waited for fate to bring lunch. The sand, which has no mouth, still managed to look disappointed in me.
entries.sceneFit: The frogfish's braced pectoral fins on bare sand make the stalled walk visible.
entries.payoffReview: The physical fact carries the joke: a hunter built for waiting mistakes immobility for a plan.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: Orange, Entirely
entries.body: I became orange in a black corner. This was not hiding. This was giving the darkness a reason to improve itself.
entries.sceneFit: The photograph is an extravagant orange frogfish isolated in black water.
entries.payoffReview: A small, image-native grandiosity. His camouflage becomes a failed demand for an audience.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: Nearly Perfect
entries.body: a snail settled beside me on the red wall. We were indistinguishable except that it had somewhere to be.
entries.sceneFit: The frogfish is genuinely difficult to isolate from the red reef wall, so the camouflage rivalry is honest.
entries.payoffReview: The rival's tiny purposeful motion humiliates Frogbert's magnificent stillness.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: Publicly Frilled
entries.body: I lay down with all my decorations out. Nothing came near me, which is a kind of respect if you have standards low enough to survive.
entries.sceneFit: The broad, cream-and-magenta frogfish reads as improbably dressed and conspicuously alone on sand.
entries.payoffReview: The image lets the lonely joke land without a sentimental explanation.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: No Questions
entries.body: I was asked whether I had seen a shrimp. I had not. I had seen a future, and it was nervous.
entries.sceneFit: The upright frogfish is visibly poised with fins spread, supporting alert attention without inventing a pictured shrimp.
entries.payoffReview: Predation stays offstage. Frogbert's portentous answer is the joke, not anyone's suffering.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: The Heavy Look
entries.body: A cleaner fish said I looked tired. I said I was carrying the whole reef emotionally. It asked whether that was why I was sitting on it.
entries.sceneFit: The heavy red frogfish is unmistakably settled on reef rubble, giving the retort a literal target.
entries.payoffReview: His melodrama gets punctured by the landscape beneath him.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: Mouth Set
entries.body: i practiced looking harmless until my face got stuck in contempt. This is why prey should not be allowed to have instincts.
entries.sceneFit: The frontal downturned mouth and fixed gaze directly support the failed harmless expression.
entries.payoffReview: The flaw is Frogbert's expression, not the prey's fear.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: A Smaller Silence
entries.body: The reef went quiet around me. I took this as devotion until a passing crab explained the concept of an ambush.
entries.sceneFit: The close, still portrait visibly makes a held silence the scene rather than an abstract claim.
entries.payoffReview: His need to be adored collides with the plain biological fact of why everyone is quiet.

entries.subject: frogfish underwater
entries.title: Side Profile
entries.body: i turned sideways for a better silhouette. A wrasse passed. I let it go. Beauty requires sacrifices, apparently from me.
entries.sceneFit: The reef-pressed side profile is the entire physical premise.
entries.payoffReview: A tiny romance-adjacent restraint with Frogbert's selfish accounting, not another mouth joke.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: One Eye's Verdict
entries.body: I made my whole body into rock except for one eye. The eye voted to leave. The rest of me had already signed eight copies of the lease in suction.
entries.sceneFit: The photo visibly hides the animal in sand and algae while leaving one bright eye exposed.
entries.payoffReview: Alma's controlling attachment becomes physically distributed dissent, grounded in the visible concealment.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: The Low Roof
entries.body: The ledge was so low I had to flatten my thoughts to get beneath it. Then a crab walked past the entrance and I became, regrettably, a person with a door policy.
entries.sceneFit: The octopus is genuinely tucked beneath a very low rock ledge with arms across the threshold.
entries.payoffReview: It starts in strange embodiment and turns into Alma's unflattering urge to control a boundary.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: Eight Opinions
entries.body: One arm wanted the sand. Seven voted for the crevice. We compromised by making the first arm look reckless.
entries.sceneFit: One arm visibly reaches from the crevice into open sand.
entries.payoffReview: The photograph supplies the split decision. The comic turn is Alma using a collective self to avoid responsibility.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: Excellent Disappearance
entries.body: I became exactly the color of the ledge. Nobody could find me, including the part of me still looking for approval.
entries.sceneFit: The mottled octopus disappears into the same texture and color as the ledge.
entries.payoffReview: A quiet emotional sting, earned by an image where camouflage nearly erases the speaker.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: The Unfolding
entries.body: I rose out of the sand very slowly, as though the sea had been waiting for my conclusion. It had not. A small fish passed my face and kept the only appointment that mattered.
entries.sceneFit: The upright octopus is visibly unfolding in open sand, with its arms and eye clear.
entries.payoffReview: Her grand entrance meets a world that remains usefully indifferent.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: Not A Rock
entries.body: I stayed pressed to the bottom until the bottom began taking credit for my patience. That is where I draw the line, with eight arms.
entries.sceneFit: The animal is visibly compressed into rock and sand, almost geologic.
entries.payoffReview: The metaphysical complaint arrives from a concrete image, then ends before turning into a lesson.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: The Look Back
entries.body: I put one eye around the rock to see whether the crab had returned. It had not. I still tidied the entrance. Some gestures are for the absent, which is annoying of them.
entries.sceneFit: One eye and curling arms are visibly set around the reef rock, supporting watchfulness without claiming a pictured crab.
entries.payoffReview: It continues Alma's attachment after the canon shell episode without cloning the false funeral.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: No One Asked
entries.body: I climbed above the reef and spread every arm into the current. The current did not applaud, but it did touch all eight at once. Close enough.
entries.sceneFit: The large octopus rises visibly above colorful reef growth with arms displayed in open water.
entries.payoffReview: Sensual without being coy. The emotional payoff is an unembarrassed, bodily substitute for applause.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: Cave Manners
entries.body: In the pink cave I found a stone that felt like an answer. I carried it for three breaths, then set it down. An answer that cannot stay where you put it is only a problem wearing jewelry.
entries.sceneFit: The octopus is folded into a richly pink cave setting, making the tactile, shelter-like encounter credible without asserting the stone is visible.
entries.payoffReview: A genuine change from Alma's possessiveness. The turn is specific and tactile, not a moral.

entries.subject: octopus underwater
entries.title: Uninvited Green
entries.body: A fish crossed the tire opening as if it owned the light. I almost chased it. Then I remembered I own nothing, which is why I keep such careful inventory.
entries.sceneFit: A large pale fish visibly crosses before the octopus in the opening of a discarded tire on sand.
entries.payoffReview: The other animal and tire are actually present. Alma's possessiveness becomes the laugh and a modest piece of growth.
